newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht up, interbank rate firms slightly late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht up, interbank rate firms slightly late.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed against the dollar in late active trade on Thursday in line with an easier dollar in major foreign markets, dealers said.
"Heavy dollar selling emerged throughout today as the U.S. unit softened against majors," said one dealer at a U.S. bank.
The baht rallied to 25.970/25.980 to the dollar late from 26.005/26.010 earlier, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate unchanged at 25.98 per dollar.
The stock market's sharp advance also boosted baht demand in expectation of more foreign capital inflows into the equity market, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate edged up to 11.50-12.00 percent late from 11.00-11.50 in the morning on higher demand for funds ahead of a long weekend, dealers said.
"Most banks were borrowers today to reserve money for the coming weekend. But dollar selling helped cap sharp interbank rate rise," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Friday is a Buddhist public holiday.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium eased to 12.00/13.00 satangs per dollar from 14.50/15.50 in the morning.
